title: Save & Compare Refactoring Baseline
text: vignette saves complete numerical baseline opal BET model refactoring change, compares post-refactoring build . workflow two modes controlled compare flag: compare = FALSE: Build model, evaluate fn() gr(), save outputs data/opal_baseline.rda, update dataset exposed via data(opal_baseline). compare = TRUE (default): Load opal_baseline dataset via data(opal_baseline) (local data/opal_baseline.rda file), rebuild inputs, check numerical equivalence speedup. Set flag knitting:
code: compare       <- TRUE  # Use here::here() to resolve paths from the project root reliably baseline_file            <- here::here("data", "opal_baseline.rda") baseline_data_file       <- here::here("data", "opal_baseline_data.rda") baseline_parameters_file <- here::here("data", "opal_baseline_parameters.rda") baseline_map_file        <- here::here("data", "opal_baseline_map.rda") bench_iters              <- 20

title: Save & Compare Refactoring Baseline
code: library(dplyr) library(RTMB) library(bench) library(here) library(opal) data(wcpo_bet_data) data <- wcpo_bet_data if (is.null(data$n_index)) data$n_index <- 1L if (is.null(data$cpue_data$index)) data$cpue_data$index <- rep(1L, nrow(data$cpue_data)) data(wcpo_bet_lf)  lf_wide <- wcpo_bet_lf %>%   tidyr::pivot_wider(     id_cols     = c(fishery, year, month, ts),     names_from  = bin,     values_from = value,     values_fill = 0   ) %>%   dplyr::arrange(fishery, ts)  var_adjust_scalars <- 1 / rep(1, data$n_fishery)  data <- prep_lf_data(data, lf_wide,                      lf_keep_fisheries = c(8, 9),                      lf_var_adjust     = var_adjust_scalars) data$lf_switch <- 1L data(wcpo_bet_wf)  data$wt_bin_start <- 1 data$wt_bin_width <- 1 data$n_wt         <- 200L  wf_wide <- wcpo_bet_wf |>   tidyr::pivot_wider(     id_cols     = c(fishery, year, month, ts),     names_from  = bin,     values_from = value,     values_fill = 0   ) |>   dplyr::arrange(fishery, ts)  data <- prep_wf_data(data, wf_wide,                      wf_keep_fisheries = c(2),                      wf_switch = 1L)

title: Save & Compare Refactoring Baseline
code: data(wcpo_bet_parameters)  parameters <- list(   log_B0         = 20,   log_h          = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_h),   log_sigma_r    = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_sigma_r),   log_cpue_q     = rep(as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_cpue_q), data$n_index),   cpue_creep     = rep(as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$cpue_creep), data$n_index),   log_cpue_tau   = rep(as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_cpue_tau), data$n_index),   log_cpue_omega = rep(as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_cpue_omega), data$n_index),   log_lf_tau     = log(rep(0.1, data$n_fishery)),   log_wf_tau     = rep(0, data$n_fishery),   log_L1         = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_L1),   log_L2         = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_L2),   log_k          = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_k),   log_CV1        = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_CV1),   log_CV2        = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_CV2),   par_sel        = as.matrix(wcpo_bet_parameters$par_sel),   rdev_y         = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$rdev_y) ) data$priors <- get_priors(parameters = parameters, data = data) map_sel <- matrix(NA, nrow(parameters$par_sel), ncol(parameters$par_sel))  map <- list(   log_h          = factor(NA),   log_sigma_r    = factor(NA),   cpue_creep     = factor(rep(NA, data$n_index)),   log_cpue_tau   = factor(rep(NA, data$n_index)),   log_cpue_omega = factor(rep(NA, data$n_index)),   log_lf_tau     = factor(rep(NA, length(parameters$log_lf_tau))),   log_wf_tau     = factor(rep(NA, length(parameters$log_wf_tau))),   log_L1         = factor(NA),   log_L2         = factor(NA),   log_k          = factor(NA),   log_CV1        = factor(NA),   log_CV2        = factor(NA),   par_sel        = factor(map_sel) ) t_build <- system.time({   obj <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data),                    parameters = parameters, map = map) }) cat("MakeADFun build time:", round(t_build["elapsed"], 2), "sec\n") cat("Estimated parameters:", length(obj$par), "\n")

")     cat("  Using relaxed tolerance:", format(tol, scientific = TRUE), "

")   all_pass <- TRUE   for (nm in names(checks)) {     val  <- checks[[nm]]     pass <- val < tol     flag <- ifelse(pass, "OK", "FAIL")     cat(sprintf("  %-22s %12.2e  [%s]
", nm, val, flag))     if (!pass) all_pass <- FALSE   }   cat("

mu_len) / sd_len       Upr[idx[1]] <- (200  - mu_len) / sd_len     }      if (!is.na(idx[2])) {       Lwr[idx[2]] <- -7       Upr[idx[2]] <-  7     }      # for sel_double_normal using exp(c)*sd^2 and exp(d)*sd^2:     # keep widths positive on a practical natural scale while avoiding     # artificial convergence on the transformed denominator bound.     shift <- 2 * log(sd_len)     width_log_lower <- log(4)     width_log_upper <- 8     if (!is.na(idx[3])) {       Lwr[idx[3]] <- width_log_lower - shift       Upr[idx[3]] <-  width_log_upper - shift     }     if (!is.na(idx[4])) {       Lwr[idx[4]] <- width_log_lower - shift       Upr[idx[4]] <-  width_log_upper - shift     }      if (!is.na(idx[5])) {       Lwr[idx[5]] <- -9 # practical bound (instead of -999)       Upr[idx[5]] <-  9     }     if (!is.na(idx[6])) {       Lwr[idx[6]] <- -9       Upr[idx[6]] <-  9     }   } }  bounds <- data.frame(par = par_labels, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr)

code: if (data$cpue_switch == 0) {   cat("CPUE likelihood is switched off (cpue_switch = 0), so no simulated CPUE to show.\n") } else {   cpue_rep <- obj$report(obj$env$last.par.best)   cpue_indices <- sort(unique(data$cpue_data$index))   cpue_months <- sort(unique(data$cpue_data$month))   cpue_index_labels <- setNames(     paste0("Month: ", cpue_months),     as.character(seq_along(cpue_months))   )    cpue_df <- data$cpue_data %>%     mutate(       obs_id = row_number(),       observed = log(value),       predicted = log(cpue_rep$cpue_pred),       index = factor(index, levels = cpue_indices,                      labels = cpue_index_labels[as.character(cpue_indices)])     )    n_sim <- 10   cpue_sim_df <- map_dfr(seq_len(n_sim), function(s) {     tibble(       obs_id = cpue_df$obs_id,       year = cpue_df$year,       index = cpue_df$index,       sim_id = s,       simulated = obj$simulate(obj$env$last.par.best)$cpue_log_obs     )   })    ggplot(cpue_df, aes(x = year)) +     geom_line(data = cpue_sim_df, aes(y = simulated, group = sim_id),               colour = "grey70", alpha = 0.55, linewidth = 0.35) +     geom_point(aes(y = observed), colour = "black", size = 1) +     geom_line(aes(y = predicted), colour = "red3", linewidth = 0.8) +     facet_wrap(~ index, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +     labs(x = "Year", y = "log(CPUE)",          subtitle = paste0(n_sim, " fitted-model simulations in grey")) +     theme_minimal() }

cat("This diagnostic chunk currently supports multinomial LF/WF likelihoods (switch = 1).\n") } else {   normalise_composition <- function(x) {     total <- sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)     if (!is.finite(total) || total <= 0) {       return(rep(NA_real_, length(x)))     }     x / total   }    quiet_comp_residual_warnings <- function(expr) {     withCallingHandlers(       expr,       warning = function(w) {         if (grepl("NA/NaN function evaluation", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {           invokeRestart("muffleWarning")         }       }     )   }    ts_to_decimal_year <- function(ts, first_yr = data$first_yr,                                  n_season = data$n_season) {     first_yr + (as.integer(ts) - 1L) %/% n_season +       ((as.integer(ts) - 1L) %% n_season) / n_season   }    flat_to_count_list <- function(v, n_f, fishery_f, minbin, maxbin) {     out <- vector("list", length(n_f))     offset <- 0L     for (k in seq_along(n_f)) {       f <- fishery_f[k]       nbins <- maxbin[f] - minbin[f] + 1L       n_values <- n_f[k] * nbins       out[[k]] <- matrix(         v[seq.int(offset + 1L, length.out = n_values)],         nrow = n_f[k],         ncol = nbins,         byrow = TRUE       )       offset <- offset + n_values     }     out   }    composition_residual_rows <- function(type_label, y_label, obs_flat,                                         pred_list, n_by_row, n_f, fishery_f,                                         year_fi, minbin, maxbin, bins) {     obs_list <- flat_to_count_list(obs_flat, n_f, fishery_f, minbin, maxbin)     row_offset <- 0L      map_dfr(seq_along(pred_list), function(i) {       f <- fishery_f[i]       n_rows <- n_f[i]       row_ids <- seq.int(row_offset + 1L, length.out = n_rows)       row_offset <<- row_offset + n_rows       active_bins <- bins[minbin[f]:maxbin[f]]       pred <- pred_list[[i]]       obs <- obs_list[[i]]       years <- year_fi[[as.character(f)]]        map_dfr(seq_len(n_rows), function(j) {         obs_prop <- normalise_composition(obs[j, ])         pred_prop <- normalise_composition(pred[j, ])         n_eff <- n_by_row[row_ids[j]]          if (anyNA(obs_prop) || anyNA(pred_prop) ||             !is.finite(n_eff) || n_eff <= 0) {           return(tibble())         }          pred_prop <- pred_prop + 1e-6         pred_prop <- pred_prop / sum(pred_prop)         residual <- as.numeric(quiet_comp_residual_warnings(           compResidual::resMulti(             obs = matrix(obs_prop * n_eff, ncol = 1L),             pred = matrix(pred_prop, ncol = 1L)           )         ))         keep <- seq_along(residual)          plot_year <- years[j]         if (!is.finite(plot_year) || plot_year < 1000) {           plot_year <- ts_to_decimal_year(years[j])         }          tibble(           composition = type_label,           y_label = y_label,           fishery_num = f,           fishery = fleet_names[f],           row = row_ids[j],           year = plot_year,           bin = active_bins[keep],           observed = obs_prop[keep],           predicted = pred_prop[keep],           n_eff = n_eff,           residual = residual,           Sign = if_else(residual >= 0, "Positive", "Negative")         )       })     })   }    lf_residuals <- composition_residual_rows(     type_label = "Length",     y_label = "Length (cm)",     obs_flat = data$lf_obs_flat,     pred_list = fit_rep$lf_pred,     n_by_row = data$lf_n,     n_f = data$lf_n_f,     fishery_f = data$lf_fishery_f,     year_fi = if (!is.null(data$lf_calendar_year_fi)) data$lf_calendar_year_fi else data$lf_year_fi,     minbin = data$lf_minbin,     maxbin = data$lf_maxbin,     bins = data$len_mid   )    wf_residuals <- composition_residual_rows(     type_label = "Weight",     y_label = "Weight (kg)",     obs_flat = data$wf_obs_flat,     pred_list = fit_rep$wf_pred,     n_by_row = data$wf_n,     n_f = data$wf_n_f,     fishery_f = data$wf_fishery_f,     year_fi = if (!is.null(data$wf_calendar_year_fi)) data$wf_calendar_year_fi else data$wf_year_fi,     minbin = data$wf_minbin,     maxbin = data$wf_maxbin,     bins = data$wt_mid   )    comp_residuals <- bind_rows(lf_residuals, wf_residuals) %>%     filter(is.finite(residual)) %>%     mutate(       fishery = factor(fishery, levels = fleet_names[sort(unique(fishery_num))]),       composition = factor(composition, levels = c("Length", "Weight"))     )    residual_summary <- comp_residuals %>%     summarise(       n = n(),       mean = mean(residual),       SDNR = sd(residual),       MAR = median(abs(residual)),       max_abs = max(abs(residual)),       .by = c(composition, fishery)     ) %>%     mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))    plot_comp_bubbles <- function(plot_data, title, y_label) {     ggplot(       plot_data,       aes(x = year, y = bin, size = abs(residual), fill = Sign)     ) +       geom_point(shape = 21, alpha = 0.65, colour = "grey30", stroke = 0.08) +       facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +       scale_fill_manual(values = c(Positive = "white", Negative = "black")) +       scale_size_area(         max_size = 4,         limits = c(0, 4),         oob = scales::squish,         name = "|OSA residual|"       ) +       scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 6)) +       labs(         title = title,         x = "Year",         y = y_label,         fill = "Residual sign",         caption = "White = observed greater than predicted; black = observed less than predicted"       ) +       theme_bw() + "Length")   wf_plot_data <- filter(comp_residuals, composition == "Weight")    if (nrow(lf_plot_data) > 0L) {     print(plot_comp_bubbles(lf_plot_data, "Length Composition OSA Residuals", "Length (cm)"))   }    if (nrow(wf_plot_data) > 0L) {     print(plot_comp_bubbles(wf_plot_data, "Weight Composition OSA Residuals", "Weight (kg)"))   }    ggplot(comp_residuals, aes(sample = residual)) +     stat_qq(size = 0.45, alpha = 0.45) +     stat_qq_line(colour = "red3", linetype = "dashed") +     facet_wrap(~ composition, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +     labs(       title = "Composition OSA Q-Q Normal Check",       x = "Theoretical quantiles",       y = "Sample quantiles"     ) +     theme_bw() }

title: LF Likelihood Benchmark: Loop vs Batched
text: vignette benchmarks two implementations length-composition likelihood RTMB AD tape: Loop — old implementation: one n_age-length matrix-vector product per observation (catch_a %*% t(pla), recorded n_age × n_len scalar multiply-adds per obs CppAD tape). Batched — current implementation: one [n_obs_f × n_age] matrix multiply per fishery (catch_ya %*% t(pla)), letting BLAS handle inner loop compressing tape single DGEMM operation per fishery. Two data subsets crossed two implementations: benchmark model intentionally minimal: estimates double-normal selectivities (sel_type_f = 2) active fisheries, computes catch--age fixed baseline numbers--age estimated selectivity, evaluates LF likelihood. full population dynamics bypassed AD tape work comes selectivity--likelihood pipeline. obj$fn() obj$gr() timed bench::mark.

title: LF Likelihood Benchmark: Loop vs Batched
text: get_length_like_loop structurally identical current get_length_like except batched fishery-level matmul replaced per-observation matrix-vector product. code looked like batching optimisation.
code: get_length_like_loop <- function(lf_obs_flat, lf_obs_ints, lf_obs_prop,                                  catch_pred_fya, pla,                                  lf_n_f, lf_fishery_f, lf_year_fi, lf_n_fi,                                  lf_minbin, lf_maxbin, removal_switch_f,                                  lf_switch, n_len, n_lf, log_lf_tau) {   "[<-" <- ADoverload("[<-")   "c"   <- ADoverload("c")    n_f    <- length(lf_n_f)   lf_pred <- vector("list", n_f)   lp     <- numeric(n_lf)    if (lf_switch == 1) lf_obs_flat <- OBS(lf_obs_flat)   if (lf_switch == 2) lf_obs_prop <- OBS(lf_obs_prop)   if (lf_switch == 3) lf_obs_ints <- OBS(lf_obs_ints)    idx        <- 0L   obs_offset <- 0L    for (j in seq_len(n_f)) {     f     <- lf_fishery_f[j]     bmin  <- lf_minbin[f]     bmax  <- lf_maxbin[f]     nbins <- bmax - bmin + 1L     lf_pred[[j]] <- matrix(0, lf_n_f[j], nbins)      for (i in seq_len(lf_n_f[j])) {       idx <- idx + 1L       y   <- lf_year_fi[[j]][i]        # ---- LOOP: one [n_age]-length matvec per observation ----       catch_a <- catch_pred_fya[f, y, ]       # [n_age] row vector       pred    <- c(catch_a %*% t(pla))         # [n_len] via row × matrix       # ----------------------------------------------------------        if (bmin > 1)    pred[bmin] <- sum(pred[1:bmin])       if (bmax < n_len) pred[bmax] <- sum(pred[bmax:n_len])       pred <- pred[bmin:bmax]       pred <- pred + 1e-8       pred <- pred / sum(pred)       lf_pred[[j]][i, ] <- pred        n_i <- lf_n_fi[[j]][i]       if (removal_switch_f[f] == 0 & n_i > 0) {         if (lf_switch == 1) {           obs_i   <- lf_obs_flat[(obs_offset + 1):(obs_offset + nbins)]           lp[idx] <- -RTMB::dmultinom(x = obs_i, prob = pred, log = TRUE)         }         if (lf_switch == 2) {           obs_i   <- lf_obs_prop[(obs_offset + 1):(obs_offset + nbins)]           alpha_i <- pred * n_i * exp(log_lf_tau[f])           lp[idx] <- -RTMBdist::ddirichlet(x = obs_i, alpha = alpha_i, log = TRUE)         }         if (lf_switch == 3) {           obs_i   <- lf_obs_ints[(obs_offset + 1):(obs_offset + nbins)]           alpha_i <- pred * exp(log_lf_tau[f])           lp[idx] <- -RTMBdist::ddirmult(x = obs_i, size = n_i, alpha = alpha_i, log = TRUE)         }       }       obs_offset <- obs_offset + nbins     }   }    REPORT(lf_pred)   return(lp) }

title: ’Opakapaka case study: benchmarking opal against Stock Synthesis 3
text: vignette documents configuration, fitting, cross-platform benchmarking opal stock assessment model ’opakapaka (Pristipomoides filamentosus), Hawaiian deepwater snapper. reference model built Stock Synthesis 3 (SS3 v3.30.19) part Opaka_simulation project, provides operating model (OM) estimation model (EM). primary objective verify opal’s population dynamics engine reproduces SS3’s spawning biomass trajectory given identical inputs. secondary objective demonstrate model fit multiple data sources: index length composition data. model covers historical period 1949–2023 three fleets: commercial fishery (Comm), non-commercial fishery (Non_comm), research fishery survey (ResFish).

title: ’Opakapaka case study: benchmarking opal against Stock Synthesis 3
text: Load opal package RTMB dependency. tidyverse package used data manipulation plotting. bundled data object opaka_data contains biological parameters, catch CPUE observations, length structure, prior specifications needed opakapaka assessment model. SS3 indexes ages 0 43 (44 age classes), opal uses 1-based internal indexing. ensure growth curve, survivorship, age-structured biology vectors align correctly SS3, set A1 = 0 (anchoring Schnute growth parameterization biological age 0) redefine age_a accordingly. min_age field passed get_growth() age sequence starts 0 rather 1. Key dimensions data: Natural mortality constant across ages M = 0.135 yr−1^{-1}. Maturity follows length-based logistic curve Mat50 = 40.7 cm. length-weight relationship uses = 1.75 ×10−5\times 10^{-5} b = 2.99. Fecundity proportional body weight (SS3 option 1 = 1, b = 0). sex ratio vector (sex_ratio) set 1.0 ages. Although SS3 applies female fraction 0.5 computing SSB, scaling already implicit opal’s B0B_0 parameterization: opal defines B0B_0 female-spawning biomass (matching SS3’s reported SSB_Virgin), per-recruit spawning potential require additional sex-ratio multiplier. See dynamics diagnostic section discussion. Length composition observations loaded bundled opaka_lf long-format data object transformed model-ready arrays. Data available two fleets: Comm (fleet 1, 1949–2023) ResFish (fleet 3, 2017–2023). Fleet 2 (Non_comm) length composition data. SS3 applies bias adjustment ramp lognormal recruitment correction term, following Methot Taylor (2011). ramp reduces correction −0.5⋅σR2-0.5 \cdot \sigma_R^2 years recruitment deviations poorly informed data, preventing mean-unbiasing introducing systematic bias deviations estimated imprecisely. ramp defined four control years (ascending start, plateau start, plateau end, descending end) maximum bias adjustment fraction. Two ramps constructed: one initial age cohorts (birth years 1906–1949, applied via init_bias_adj_a) one time-series cohorts (1949–2023, applied via bias_adj_y). use SS3 EM’s estimated ramp parameters.

library(tidyverse) library(opal) library(RTMB)  theme_set(theme_bw()) data(opaka_data) data <- opaka_data if (is.null(data$n_index)) data$n_index <- 2L names(data)  # remove priors data$priors <- NULL  # set ages to anchor growth curve (since SS3 indexs from 0 to 43, but opal uses 1-based indexing) data$A1 <- 0 data$A2 <- data$A1 + (data$n_age-1) data$min_age <- 0 ages <- data$age_a <- seq(data$min_age, by = 1, length.out = data$n_age) cat("Number of ages:", data$n_age, "
") cat("Number of years:", data$n_year, "
") cat("Number of fisheries:", data$n_fishery, "
") cat("Number of length bins:", data$n_len, "
") # Natural mortality ggplot(data.frame(age = ages, M = data$M), aes(x = age, y = M)) +   geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.8) +   labs(x = "Age (opal internal)", y = "M (annual rate)",        title = "Natural Mortality-at-Age")  # Maturity at length len_mid <- seq(data$len_bin_start + data$len_bin_width / 2,                by = data$len_bin_width, length.out = data$n_len) ggplot(data.frame(length = len_mid, maturity = data$maturity),        aes(x = length, y = maturity)) +   geom_line() + geom_point() +   labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Maturity",        title = "Maturity-at-Length (logistic, Mat50 = 40.7 cm)")  # define sex ratio vector data$sex_ratio <- rep(1, data$n_age) data(opaka_lf)  # Pivot to wide format: one row per fishery x timestep, bins as columns lf_wide <- opaka_lf %>%   tidyr::pivot_wider(     id_cols = c(fishery, year, month, ts),     names_from = bin,     values_from = value,     values_fill = 0   ) %>%   arrange(fishery, ts)  # Define variance adjustment scalars for each fishery var_adjust_scalars <- 1 / rep(1, data$n_fishery)  data <- prep_lf_data(data, lf_wide,                      lf_keep_fisheries = c(1, 3),                      lf_var_adjust = var_adjust_scalars,                      lf_addtocomp = 1e-10) # 1. INITIAL COHORTS (1906 to 1949) # Data ages are 1-based, so 1949 - (age - 1) gives the birth year. # Age_a = 1 (bio age 0) -> Born in 1949. # Age_a = 44 (bio age 43) -> Born in 1906. init_cohort_years <- 1949 - (data$age_a - 1)  data$init_bias_adj_a <- get_bias_adj_vector(   years = init_cohort_years,   do_rec_bias_ramp = 1,   bias_years = c(1931, 1974, 2021.88, 2022.43),   max_bias_adj = 0.869 )  # 2. TIME SERIES COHORTS (1950 to 2024) # Because rdev_y[1] generates recruits for year 2 (1950), # the time-series bias ramp must evaluate 1950 to 2024. calendar_years <- (1949-1) + data$years  data$bias_adj_y <- get_bias_adj_vector(   years = calendar_years,   do_rec_bias_ramp = 1,   bias_years = c(1931, 1974, 2021.88, 2022.43),   max_bias_adj = 0.869 )

flat_to_list <- function(v, lf_n_f, nbins) {     out <- vector("list", length(lf_n_f))     offset <- 0L     for (k in seq_along(lf_n_f)) {       m <- matrix(v[(offset + 1):(offset + lf_n_f[k] * nbins)], nrow = lf_n_f[k], ncol = nbins, byrow = TRUE)       # Normalise each row to proportions       rs <- rowSums(m)       rs[rs == 0] <- 1       out[[k]] <- m / rs       offset <- offset + lf_n_f[k] * nbins     }     out   }    # Split year index by fishery (must match length of lf_year)   lf_year_list <- split(data$lf_year, data$lf_fishery)    # ---- Predicted: long data frame ---- as.numeric(length))   })    # ---- Observed: long data frame ----   df_obs <- data.frame(data$lf_obs_in)   names(df_obs) <- data$len_mid   df_obs <- df_obs %>%     mutate(year = data$lf_year, fishery = as.character(data$lf_fishery)) %>%     group_by(fishery) %>%     mutate(id = row_number()) %>%     ungroup() %>%     pivot_longer(cols = -c(year, fishery, id), names_to = "length", values_to = "obs") %>%     mutate(length = as.numeric(length))    # ---- Simulations: generate n_sim draws and convert to long format ----   n_sim <- 5   df_sim_all <- map_dfr(seq_len(n_sim), function(s) {     # Determine which OBS vector was active based on lf_switch     sim <- obj$simulate()     if (data$lf_switch == 1) {       sim_vec <- sim$lf_obs_flat     } else if (data$lf_switch == 2) {       sim_vec <- sim$lf_obs_prop     } else {       sim_vec <- sim$lf_obs_ints     }     sim_list <- flat_to_list(sim_vec, data$lf_n_f, nbins)     names(sim_list) <- data$lf_fishery_f     for (k in seq_along(sim_list)) colnames(sim_list[[k]]) <- data$len_mid     map_dfr(seq_along(sim_list), function(i) {       m <- sim_list[[i]]       yrs <- lf_year_list[[i]]       as.data.frame.table(m, responseName = "sim", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%         rename(id = Var1, length = Var2) %>%         mutate(fishery = names(sim_list)[i],                id = as.integer(factor(id, levels = unique(id))),                year = yrs[id],                length = as.numeric(length),                sim_id = s)     })   })    # ---- Join observed + predicted ----   df <- left_join(df_obs, df_pred, by = c("id", "fishery", "length")) %>%     select(-year.y) %>%     rename(year = year.x)    # ---- Plot fishery 1 (Comm) ----   yrs_plot_1 <- seq(from=11,to=81,by=10)   p1 <- ggplot(df %>% Name the list elements and columns   names(lf_pred) <- data$lf_fishery_f   for (k in seq_along(lf_pred)) colnames(lf_pred[[k]]) <- data$len_mid    # Helper: convert a flat OBS vector back to list-of-matrices (proportions)   flat_to_list <- function(v, lf_n_f, nbins) {     out <- vector("list", length(lf_n_f))     offset <- 0L     for (k in seq_along(lf_n_f)) {       m <- matrix(v[(offset + 1):(offset + lf_n_f[k] * nbins)], nrow = lf_n_f[k], ncol = nbins, byrow = TRUE)       # Normalise each row to proportions       rs <- rowSums(m)       rs[rs == 0] <- 1       out[[k]] <- m / rs       offset <- offset + lf_n_f[k] * nbins     }     out   }    # Split year index by fishery (must match length of lf_year)   lf_year_list <- split(data$lf_year, data$lf_fishery)    # ---- Predicted: long data frame ----   df_pred <- map_dfr(seq_along(lf_pred), function(i) {     m <- lf_pred[[i]]     yrs <- lf_year_list[[i]]     as.data.frame.table(m, responseName = "pred", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%       rename(id = Var1, length = Var2) %>%       mutate(fishery = names(lf_pred)[i],              id = as.integer(factor(id, levels = unique(id))),              year = yrs[id],              length = as.numeric(length))   })    # ---- Observed: long data frame ----   df_obs <- data.frame(data$lf_obs_in)   names(df_obs) <- data$len_mid   df_obs <- df_obs %>%     mutate(year = data$lf_year, fishery = as.character(data$lf_fishery)) %>%     group_by(fishery) %>%     mutate(id = row_number()) %>%     ungroup() %>%     pivot_longer(cols = -c(year, fishery, id), names_to = "length", values_to = "obs") %>%     mutate(length = as.numeric(length))    # ---- Simulations: generate n_sim draws and convert to long format ----   n_sim <- 5   df_sim_all <- map_dfr(seq_len(n_sim), function(s) {     # Determine which OBS vector was active based on lf_switch     sim <- obj$simulate()     if (data$lf_switch == 1) {       sim_vec <- sim$lf_obs_flat     } else if (data$lf_switch == 2) {       sim_vec <- sim$lf_obs_prop     } else {       sim_vec <- sim$lf_obs_ints     }     sim_list <- flat_to_list(sim_vec, data$lf_n_f, nbins)     names(sim_list) <- data$lf_fishery_f     for (k in seq_along(sim_list)) colnames(sim_list[[k]]) <- data$len_mid     map_dfr(seq_along(sim_list), function(i) {       m <- sim_list[[i]]       yrs <- lf_year_list[[i]]       as.data.frame.table(m, responseName = "sim", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%         rename(id = Var1, length = Var2) %>%         mutate(fishery = names(sim_list)[i],                id = as.integer(factor(id, levels = unique(id))),                year = yrs[id],                length = as.numeric(length),                sim_id = s)     })   })    # ---- Join observed + predicted ----   df <- left_join(df_obs, df_pred, by = c("id", "fishery", "length")) %>%     select(-year.y) %>%     rename(year = year.x)    # ---- Plot fishery 1 (Comm) ----   yrs_plot_1 <- seq(from=11,to=81,by=10)   p1 <- ggplot(df %>% filter(fishery == "1", year %in% yrs_plot_1), aes(x = length)) +     geom_col(aes(y = obs), fill = "grey70", width = 2) +     geom_line(data = df_sim_all %>% filter(fishery == "1", year %in% yrs_plot_1),               aes(y = sim, group = sim_id), colour = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.4) +     geom_line(aes(y = pred), colour = "red3", linewidth = 0.7) +     facet_wrap(~ year, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) +     labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Proportion",          title = "Length composition: Comm (Fishery 1)",          subtitle = "Grey bars = observed, red = predicted, blue = simulated") +     theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7),           axis.text = element_text(size = 6))   print(p1) }

Turning length composition likelihood allows data inform selectivity directly relaxes constraint. new model (obj_lf) extends obj two additional changes: lf_switch = 1L (multinomial): length composition observations Comm (fleet 1, 1949–2023) ResFish (fleet 3, 2017–2023) enter likelihood. Selectivity estimated fleets 1 3: two logistic parameters Comm six double-normal parameters ResFish freed. Fleet 2 (Non_comm) retains fixed SS3 selectivity LF data. parameters match obj: σR\sigma_R, steepness, growth remain fixed SS3 values; B0B_0, catchabilities, rdev_y, init_rdev_a freely estimated.
code: # data_no_sel has no sel_fa_external (set in dynamics-check); use it as base data_lf <- data_no_sel data_lf$lf_switch <- 1L  map_sel <- matrix(NA, nrow(parameters$par_sel), ncol(parameters$par_sel)) map_sel[1,1:2 ] <- c(1,2) # Comm fleet selectivity parameters map_sel[3,c(1,4,6) ] <- c(3,4,5) # Comm fleet selectivity parameters map_sel = as.vector(map_sel)  map_lf <- map map_lf$par_sel <- factor(map_sel) obj_lf <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data_lf),                     parameters = parameters,                     map = map_lf) unique(names(obj_lf$par)) obj_lf$fn()   # should be finite Lwr_lf <- rep(-Inf, length(obj_lf$par)) Upr_lf <- rep( Inf, length(obj_lf$par))  Lwr_lf[grep("log_B0",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(1) Upr_lf[grep("log_B0",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(exp(22)) Lwr_lf[grep("log_cpue_q",  names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(0.001) Upr_lf[grep("log_cpue_q",  names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(10) Lwr_lf[grep("rdev_y",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- -5 Upr_lf[grep("rdev_y",      names(obj_lf$par))] <-  5 Lwr_lf[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_lf$par))] <- -5 Upr_lf[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_lf$par))] <-  5 Lwr_lf[grep("par_sel",     names(obj_lf$par))] <- -7 Upr_lf[grep("par_sel",     names(obj_lf$par))] <-  7 control <- list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000) opt_lf <- nlminb(start = obj_lf$par, objective = obj_lf$fn,                  gradient = obj_lf$gr, lower = Lwr_lf, upper = Upr_lf,                  control = control) opt_lf <- nlminb(start = opt_lf$par, objective = obj_lf$fn, 1e-2, digits = 2L,include="all_est") lf_rep_lf  <- obj_lf$report() lf_pred_lf <- lf_rep_lf$lf_pred  names(lf_pred_lf) <- data_lf$lf_fishery_f for (k in seq_along(lf_pred_lf)) colnames(lf_pred_lf[[k]]) <- data_lf$len_mid  lf_year_list_lf <- split(data_lf$lf_year, data_lf$lf_fishery)  df_pred_lf <- map_dfr(seq_along(lf_pred_lf), function(i) {   m   <- lf_pred_lf[[i]]   yrs <- lf_year_list_lf[[i]]   as.data.frame.table(m, responseName = "pred", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%     rename(id = Var1, length = Var2) %>%     mutate(fishery = as.character(names(lf_pred_lf)[i]),            id      = as.integer(factor(id, levels = unique(id))),            year    = yrs[id],            length  = as.numeric(length)) })  df_obs_lf <- data.frame(data_lf$lf_obs_in) names(df_obs_lf) <- data_lf$len_mid df_obs_lf <- df_obs_lf %>%   mutate(year = data_lf$lf_year, fishery = as.character(data_lf$lf_fishery)) %>%   group_by(fishery) %>%   mutate(id = row_number()) %>%   ungroup() %>%   pivot_longer(cols = -c(year, fishery, id), names_to = "length", values_to = "obs") %>%   mutate(length = as.numeric(length))  df_lf <- left_join(df_obs_lf, df_pred_lf, by = c("id", "fishery", "length")) %>%   select(-year.y) %>%   rename(year = year.x) %>%   mutate(cal_year = 1948L + year)   # convert model timestep to calendar year  # Fleet 1 (Comm): every 10 timesteps ts_comm <- ts_comm), aes(x = length)) +   geom_col(aes(y = obs), fill = "grey70", width = 2) +   geom_line(aes(y = pred), colour = "cyan4", linewidth = 0.8) +   facet_wrap(~cal_year, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) 7), axis.text = element_text(size = 6)) print(p_comm)  # Fleet 3 (ResFish): all available timesteps ts_res <- sort(unique(data_lf$lf_year[data_lf$lf_fishery == 3])) p_res <- ggplot(df_lf %>% filter(fishery == "3", year %in% ts_res), aes(x = length)) +   geom_col(aes(y = obs), fill = "grey70", width = 2) +   geom_line(aes(y = pred), colour = "cyan4", linewidth = 0.8) +   facet_wrap(~cal_year, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +   labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Proportion",        title = "Length composition fit: ResFish (Fleet 3)",        subtitle = "Grey = observed, cyan = predicted") +   theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7), axis.text = element_text(size = 6)) print(p_res) par_sel_lf  <- obj_lf$env$parList()$par_sel par_sel_obj <- obj$env$parList()$par_sel  sel_comp_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(data_lf$n_fishery), function(f) {   sel_lf_l <- if (data_lf$sel_type_f[f] == 1L) {     sel_logistic(data_lf$len_mid, par_sel_lf[f, ])   } else {     sel_double_normal(data_lf$len_mid, par_sel_lf[f, ])   }   sel_obj_l <- if (data$sel_type_f[f] == 1L) {     sel_logistic(data$len_mid, par_sel_obj[f, ])   } else {     sel_double_normal(data$len_mid, par_sel_obj[f, ])   }   rbind(     data.frame(fleet = fleet_names[f], length = data_lf$len_mid,                selectivity = as.numeric(sel_lf_l),  model = "opal (with LF)"),     data.frame(fleet = fleet_names[f], length = data$len_mid,                selectivity = as.numeric(sel_obj_l), model = "opal (ASPM-R)")   ) }))  ggplot(sel_comp_df, aes(x = length, y = selectivity, colour = model)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +   facet_wrap(~fleet, ncol = 3) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("opal (with LF)" = "cyan4",                                  "opal (ASPM-R)"  = "purple")) +   labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Selectivity",        title = "Selectivity-at-length: ASPM-R vs model with LF",        colour = NULL) +   ylim(0, 1) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") rep_lf <- obj_lf$report()  ssb_lf_df <- data.frame(   year     = calendar_years,   estimate = rep_lf$spawning_biomass_y[1:data$n_year],   model    = "opal (with LF)" )  ssb_df_all <- rbind(ssb_df_est, ssb_lf_df)  ybmax_all <- max(ssb_df_all$estimate,                  opaka_truth$om$sprseries$SSB,                  opaka_truth$em$sprseries$SSB,                  na.rm = TRUE)  ggplot() +   geom_line(data = ssb_df_all,             aes(x = year, y = estimate, colour = model), linewidth = 1) +   geom_line(data = subset(opaka_truth$om$sprseries, Yr %in% calendar_years),             aes(x = Yr, y = SSB, colour = "SS3 OM"), linewidth = 1) +   geom_line(data = subset(opaka_truth$em$sprseries, Yr %in% calendar_years),             aes(x = Yr, y = SSB, colour = "SS3 EM"), linewidth = 1) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c(     "opal (PLA selectivity; scale fixed)"     = "steelblue",     "opal (SS3 selectivity; scale fixed)"     = "darkorange",     "opal (PLA selectivity; scale estimated)" = "green4",     "opal (ASPM-R)"                           = "purple",     "opal (with LF)"                          = "cyan4",     "SS3 OM"                                  = "black",     "SS3 EM"                                  = "red"   )) +   labs(x = "Year", y = "Spawning biomass",        title = "Full model comparison",        subtitle = "Fixed diagnostics \u2192 ASPM-R \u2192 model with LF + estimated selectivity",        colour = NULL) +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, ybmax_all * 1.2)) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "right")

title: Profiling & Benchmarking
text: profvis samples R call stack regular intervals produces interactive flame graph. Run 10 iterations fn() + gr() accumulate enough samples: Open profile_full.html browser inspect flame graph. Key things look : Time get_harvest_rate vs do_dynamics vs opal_model — get_harvest_rate significant fraction, Change 1 (inlining) help. Time get_length_like / get_weight_like / get_cpue_like — composition likelihoods dominate, Changes 7–9 important. weight likelihood adds extra rebinning matrix multiply per observation. Time getAll() calls — indicates overhead unpacking data/parameter lists. Time .Call (C++ / RTMB internals) vs R code — time .Call, bottleneck tape complexity rather R dispatch overhead.
code: prof <- profvis({   for (i in 1:10) {     obj$fn(obj$par)     obj$gr(obj$par)   } }, simplify = FALSE)  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(prof, "profile_full.html", selfcontained = TRUE)

title: Profiling & Benchmarking
text: Uncomment block time full nlminb optimisation run. useful measuring end--end improvement takes several minutes:
code:
Lwr <- rep(-Inf, length(obj$par)) Upr <- rep(Inf, length(obj$par)) Lwr[grep("log_B0", names(obj$par))] <- log(1) Upr[grep("log_B0", names(obj$par))] <- log(exp(22)) Lwr[grep("log_cpue_q", names(obj$par))] <- log(0.1) Upr[grep("log_cpue_q", names(obj$par))] <- log(10) Lwr[grep("rdev_y", names(obj$par))] <- -5 Upr[grep("rdev_y", names(obj$par))] <- 5  control <- list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000)  t_opt <- system.time({   opt <- nlminb(start = obj$par, objective = obj$fn, gradient = obj$gr,                 hessian = obj$he, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr, control = control) }) cat("Optimization time: ", round(t_opt["elapsed"], 1), "sec
") cat("Convergence:       ", ifelse(opt$convergence == 0, "TRUE", "FALSE"), "
") cat("Final NLL:         ", round(opt$objective, 4), "
") cat("Function evals:    ", opt$evaluations["function"], "
") cat("Gradient evals:    ", opt$evaluations["gradient"], "
") cat("Sec per fn eval:   ", round(t_opt["elapsed"] / opt$evaluations["function"], 4), "
") cat("Sec per gr eval:   ", round(t_opt["elapsed"] / opt$evaluations["gradient"], 4), "
")

title: Projections and uncertainty: MVN vs MCMC
text: vignette demonstrates full simulation-estimation-projection workflow opal: Fit model real data (WCPO bigeye tuna, CPUE likelihood ). Construct alternative catch scenario fishing effort reduced 50 % last 20 years, producing biomass recovery signal. Simulate synthetic CPUE series recovery scenario, using original MLE parameters modified catch — establishing known “truth”. Refit model simulated data MVN MCMC approaches evaluated known trajectory. MVN simulation — multivariate-normal draws Hessian-derived variance-covariance matrix; MCMC required. MCMC posteriors — draws posterior distribution obtained via SparseNUTS (code shown; set eval: true chunks run). Compare resulting uncertainty envelopes true simulated trajectory. See vignette("bet") detailed walkthrough BET model setup.

title: Projections and uncertainty: MVN vs MCMC
text: Fix parameters except log_B0, log_cpue_q, recruitment deviates rdev_y. Deviates first generation time fixed zero — population near unfished state period catch information distinguish individual year-class strengths.
code: library(opal) library(RTMB) library(SparseNUTS) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(knitr) library(posterior)  theme_set(theme_bw())  # The MCMC fit is pre-computed and loaded from the package (the `mcmc-sampling` # chunk that would produce it is disabled); n_chains_mcmc must match the number # of chains used to produce the cached fit. n_chains_mcmc <- 8L mcmc_fit <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "mcmc_fit.rds", package = "opal")) data(wcpo_bet_data) data(wcpo_bet_parameters)  data <- wcpo_bet_data  # Use CPUE likelihood only for speed data$lf_switch   <- 0L data$wf_switch   <- 0L data$cpue_switch <- 1L  # Length bin bounds and midpoints (required by the PLA inside the model) data$len_lower <- seq(from = data$len_bin_start, by = data$len_bin_width,                       length.out = data$n_len) data$len_upper <- data$len_lower + data$len_bin_width data$len_mid   <- data$len_lower + data$len_bin_width / 2  # Removal switch: 0 = fishery active (required by project_selectivity) data$removal_switch_f <- rep(0L, data$n_fishery) parameters <- list(   log_B0         = 20,   log_h          = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_h),   log_sigma_r    = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_sigma_r),   log_cpue_q     = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_cpue_q),   cpue_creep     = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$cpue_creep),   log_cpue_tau   = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_cpue_tau),   log_cpue_omega = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_cpue_omega),   log_lf_tau     = log(rep(0.1, data$n_fishery)),   log_wf_tau     = rep(0, data$n_fishery),   log_L1         = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_L1),   log_L2         = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_L2),   log_k          = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_k),   log_CV1        = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_CV1),   log_CV2        = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$log_CV2),   par_sel        = as.matrix(wcpo_bet_parameters$par_sel),   rdev_y         = as.numeric(wcpo_bet_parameters$rdev_y) ) # Build a temporary model to extract life-history arrays for generation-time # calculation; no optimisation is performed here. obj_tmp <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data), parameters = parameters,                      map = list(                        log_h=factor(NA), log_sigma_r=factor(NA), log_B0=factor(NA),                        cpue_creep=factor(NA), log_cpue_tau=factor(NA),                        log_cpue_omega=factor(NA),                        log_lf_tau=factor(rep(NA,data$n_fishery)),                        log_wf_tau=factor(rep(NA,data$n_fishery)),                        log_L1=factor(NA), log_L2=factor(NA), log_k=factor(NA),                        log_CV1=factor(NA), log_CV2=factor(NA),                        log_cpue_q=factor(NA),                        par_sel=factor(matrix(NA,nrow(parameters$par_sel),                                                 ncol(parameters$par_sel))),                        rdev_y=factor(rep(NA, length(parameters$rdev_y)))                      )) rep_tmp <- obj_tmp$report()  # Generation time = mean age of spawners at unfished equilibrium (0-based ages) M_a_tmp   <- as.numeric(rep_tmp$M_a) spa_tmp   <- as.numeric(rep_tmp$spawning_potential_a) n_age_tmp <- length(M_a_tmp) surv_tmp  <- numeric(n_age_tmp) surv_tmp[1] <- 1 for (a in seq(2, n_age_tmp))   surv_tmp[a] <- surv_tmp[a - 1] * exp(-M_a_tmp[a - 1]) surv_tmp[n_age_tmp] <- surv_tmp[n_age_tmp] / (1 - exp(-M_a_tmp[n_age_tmp])) ages_0based <- seq_len(n_age_tmp) - 1 spa_w <- spa_tmp * surv_tmp n_gen <- round(sum(ages_0based * spa_w) / sum(spa_w)) rm(obj_tmp, rep_tmp, M_a_tmp, spa_tmp, surv_tmp, spa_w, ages_0based, n_age_tmp) map <- list(   log_h          = factor(NA),   log_sigma_r    = factor(NA),   cpue_creep     = factor(NA),   log_cpue_tau   = factor(NA),   log_cpue_omega = factor(NA),   log_lf_tau     = factor(rep(NA, data$n_fishery)),   log_wf_tau     = factor(rep(NA, data$n_fishery)),   log_L1         = factor(NA),   log_L2         = factor(NA),   log_k          = factor(NA),   log_CV1        = factor(NA),   log_CV2        = factor(NA),   par_sel        = factor(matrix(NA, nrow(parameters$par_sel),                                      ncol(parameters$par_sel))),   # Fix the first n_gen rdev_y to zero (unfished spin-up period)   rdev_y         = factor(c(rep(NA, n_gen),                             seq_len(data$n_year - n_gen))) ) obj <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data), parameters = parameters, map = map)  Lwr <- rep(-Inf, length(obj$par)) Upr <- rep( Inf, length(obj$par)) Lwr[grep("log_B0",     names(obj$par))] <- log(1) Upr[grep("log_B0",     names(obj$par))] <- log(exp(22)) Lwr[grep("log_cpue_q", names(obj$par))] <- log(0.1) Upr[grep("log_cpue_q", names(obj$par))] <- log(10) Lwr[grep("rdev_y",     names(obj$par))] <- -5 Upr[grep("rdev_y",     names(obj$par))] <-  5  control <- list(eval.max = 5000, iter.max = 5000) opt <- nlminb(start = obj$par, objective = obj$fn, gradient = obj$gr,               lower = Lwr, upper = Upr, control = control) opt <- nlminb(start = opt$par, objective = obj$fn, gradient = obj$gr,               lower = Lwr, upper = Upr, control = control)  cat("Max gradient:", max(abs(obj$gr())), "\n") cat("NLL:", opt$objective, "\n")

title: Projections and uncertainty: MVN vs MCMC
text: give model distinctive informative signal current stock state, modify catch time-series last 80 quarters (20 years) effort declines linearly 50 % original level terminal quarter. resulting biomass recovery produces rising CPUE trend constrains current state tightly, reducing posterior uncertainty leading closer agreement MVN MCMC projections. Simulate one CPUE realisation recovery scenario. build AD object modified catch, evaluate original MLE parameter vector (opt$par) simulated trajectory reflects recovery parameters, draw single CPUE realisation: Compare original simulated CPUE series — rising trend final 20 years recovery signal want model detect:
code: data_alt <- data n_yr     <- data$n_year  for (y in seq(n_yr - 79L, n_yr)) {   # Linear ramp from 100 % (quarter n_yr − 79) to 50 % (terminal quarter)   frac <- 1 - 0.5 * (y - (n_yr - 80L)) / 80   data_alt$catch_obs_ysf[y, , ] <- data$catch_obs_ysf[y, , ] * frac } catch_orig <- rowSums(data$catch_obs_ysf,     dims = 1) catch_alt  <- rowSums(data_alt$catch_obs_ysf, dims = 1) years_all  <- seq_len(n_yr) plot(years_all, catch_orig, type = "l", col = "grey50", lwd = 1,      xlab = "Quarter", ylab = "Total catch (mt)") lines(years_all, catch_alt, col = "steelblue", lwd = 1.5) abline(v = n_yr - 79, lty = 2, col = "grey70") legend("topright", c("Original", "Reduced (recovery scenario)"),        col = c("grey50", "steelblue"), lwd = c(1, 1.5)) # Build model object with modified catch obj_alt <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data_alt), parameters = parameters,                      map = map)  # Evaluate at original MLE so internal state = recovery trajectory invisible(obj_alt$fn(opt$par))  # True SSB trajectory under the recovery scenario (the "ground truth") rep_true_alt <- obj_alt$report() sbio_true    <- rep_true_alt$spawning_biomass_y   # length n_year + 1  # Draw one CPUE realisation consistent with the recovery trajectory set.seed(42) sim_alt <- obj_alt$simulate()  # Use modified catch + simulated CPUE as the scenario data data_sim <- data_alt data_sim$cpue_data$value <- exp(sim_alt$cpue_log_obs) plot(data$cpue_data$value, type = "l", col = "grey50", lwd = 1,      xlab = "Time step", ylab = "CPUE") lines(data_sim$cpue_data$value, col = "steelblue", lwd = 1.5) abline(v = n_yr - 79, lty = 2, col = "grey70") legend("topright", c("Original observed", "Recovery scenario"),        col = c("grey50", "steelblue"), lwd = c(1, 1.5))

title: Projections and uncertainty: MVN vs MCMC
text: Build new AD object simulated data re-optimise original starting values. recovers parameters consistent simulated observations gives us known “truth” projection comparison: Add data-driven prior centres using refitted MLE estimates, rebuild obj_sim AD tape carries priors MCMC sampling: Compute Hessian-based standard errors derived quantities via delta method. used later draw historical uncertainty ribbon: Compare true recovery-scenario trajectory trajectory estimated refitting simulated data. Close agreement shows model can recover true trajectory simulated observations:
code: obj_sim <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data_sim),                      parameters = parameters, map = map)  opt_sim <- nlminb(start = obj_sim$par, objective = obj_sim$fn,                   gradient = obj_sim$gr,                   lower = Lwr, upper = Upr, control = control) opt_sim <- nlminb(start = opt_sim$par, objective = obj_sim$fn,                   gradient = obj_sim$gr,                   lower = Lwr, upper = Upr, control = control)  cat("Max gradient (refitted):", max(abs(obj_sim$gr())), "\n") # Prior centres anchored to the refitted MLE (avoids the default par1=0 for # log_B0 which would be wildly wrong for a stock of this size) data_sim$prior_log_B0_mean     <- opt_sim$par["log_B0"] data_sim$prior_log_cpue_q_mean <- opt_sim$par["log_cpue_q"]  # Build the priors list using the full structured parameters list so that # get_priors() produces indices that match the RTMB AD tape layout. # The data-driven centres above are used by get_priors(); the parameter # values themselves only serve as fallback and do not matter here. data_sim$priors <- get_priors(parameters, data_sim)  # Rebuild obj_sim with updated data (AD tape must capture data$priors) obj_sim <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data_sim),                      parameters = parameters, map = map) invisible(obj_sim$fn(opt_sim$par)) # ADREPORT(spawning_biomass_y) is registered inside do_dynamics(), so sdreport # propagates Hessian uncertainty through the full historical trajectory via # automatic differentiation. sdr_sim   <- RTMB::sdreport(obj_sim) sdr_sum   <- summary(sdr_sim, "report") sbio_rows <- which(rownames(sdr_sum) == "spawning_biomass_y") sbio_mle_sd <- sdr_sum[sbio_rows, "Estimate"] sbio_se_sd  <- sdr_sum[sbio_rows, "Std. Error"] rep_sim  <- obj_sim$report()  ylim <- range(c(sbio_true, rep_sim$spawning_biomass_y)) * c(0, 1.15) plot(sbio_true, type = "l", col = "black", lwd = 2, lty = 2,      ylim = ylim,      xlab = "Time step", ylab = "Spawning biomass (mt)") lines(rep_sim$spawning_biomass_y, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2) legend("topright", c("True (recovery scenario)", "Refitted MLE"),        col = c("black", "steelblue"), lwd = 2, lty = c(2, 1))

title: Projections and uncertainty: MVN vs MCMC
text: refitted model three groups free parameters: unfished spawning biomass (log_B0), CPUE catchability coefficient (log_cpue_q), annual log-recruitment deviates (rdev_y). Standard errors computed square root diagonal inverse Hessian MLE. recruitment deviates rdev_y cover model years, first generation-time block fixed zero — population assumed unfished equilibrium spin-period. remaining deviates freely estimated, centred zero recruitment standard deviation prior.
code: H_sim   <- obj_sim$he() Sigma   <- solve(H_sim) SE_vec  <- sqrt(diag(Sigma)) mu_vec  <- obj_sim$env$last.par.best  # Extract scalar free parameters and convert to natural scale scalar_params <- data.frame(   Parameter  = c("B0 (mt)", "CPUE q"),   MLE        = c(exp(mu_vec["log_B0"]),                  exp(mu_vec["log_cpue_q"])),   SE_log     = c(SE_vec[names(mu_vec) == "log_B0"][1],                  SE_vec[names(mu_vec) == "log_cpue_q"][1]),   CI_lo95    = c(exp(mu_vec["log_B0"]  - 1.96 * SE_vec[names(mu_vec) == "log_B0"][1]),                  exp(mu_vec["log_cpue_q"] - 1.96 * SE_vec[names(mu_vec) == "log_cpue_q"][1])),   CI_hi95    = c(exp(mu_vec["log_B0"]  + 1.96 * SE_vec[names(mu_vec) == "log_B0"][1]),                  exp(mu_vec["log_cpue_q"] + 1.96 * SE_vec[names(mu_vec) == "log_cpue_q"][1])) ) scalar_params[, 2:5] <- round(scalar_params[, 2:5], 4) scalar_params$MLE[1]     <- round(scalar_params$MLE[1]) scalar_params$CI_lo95[1] <- round(scalar_params$CI_lo95[1]) scalar_params$CI_hi95[1] <- round(scalar_params$CI_hi95[1]) knitr::kable(scalar_params,              col.names = c("Parameter", "MLE", "SE (log scale)", "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper"),              caption   = "MLE estimates and Hessian-based 95% confidence intervals.") rdev_idx <- which(names(mu_vec) == "rdev_y") rdev_mle_est <- mu_vec[rdev_idx] rdev_se_est  <- SE_vec[rdev_idx] # Reconstruct full time-series: fixed years = 0 (SE = 0), estimated years free rdev_mle <- c(rep(0, n_gen), rdev_mle_est) rdev_se  <- c(rep(0, n_gen), rdev_se_est) rdev_df  <- data.frame(   year  = seq_len(data_sim$n_year),   rdev  = rdev_mle,   lo95  = rdev_mle - 1.96 * rdev_se,   hi95  = rdev_mle + 1.96 * rdev_se,   fixed = c(rep(TRUE, n_gen), rep(FALSE, data_sim$n_year - n_gen)) ) ggplot(rdev_df, aes(x = year)) +   annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = n_gen + 0.5,            ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.6) +   geom_ribbon(data = subset(rdev_df, !fixed),               aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +   geom_line(aes(y = rdev), colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.6) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +   labs(x = "Model year", y = "log-recruitment deviate")

title: Projections and uncertainty: MVN vs MCMC
text: mcmc = NULL, project_dynamics() samples parameter sets multivariate-normal distribution centred MLE, using inverse Hessian covariance matrix. sampling performed working (unconstrained) scales — log positive parameters, logit autocorrelation parameters — covariance adjusted via delta method, back-transformed native parameter space call obj$report(). Run -U-Turn sampler (NUTS) chain via SparseNUTS. opal_globals() call exports helper functions needed likelihood evaluation inside MCMC workers. MCMC path, projected recruitment deviates generated fitting ARIMA model posterior draw’s historical rdev_y series. keeps projected rdev pattern consistent historical rdev pattern draw — ARIMA structure characterises, say, high-recruitment draw historical period also governs projection. MVN path (), ARIMA fitted single MLE series, appropriate MVN iterations share conditional-expectation history. comparing projection envelopes, check whether NUTS chains converged. 1000 warmup steps 8 independent chains, dense-metric SparseNUTS sampler adapts full Hessian-based mass matrix captures correlations B0, q, rdev_y parameters 270-dimensional parameter space. Split-chain Rhat per-chain ESS provide reliable convergence diagnostics across chains. Without informative priors log_B0 log_cpue_q, joint likelihood ridge: high B0B_0 paired low qq fits CPUE well low B0B_0 high qq. MCMC correctly samples flat posterior, posterior mean can lie far MLE (sits mode). Enabling data-driven priors (centred refitted MLE) regularises posterior toward MLE. prior vs posterior comparison illustrates .
code: n_proj <- 10   # projection quarters n_iter <- 200  # uncertainty iterations  # Projected recruitment deviates — ARIMA-based simulation from the fitted series rdev_proj <- project_rec_devs(   data     = data_sim,   obj      = obj_sim,   first_yr = data_sim$first_yr,   n_proj   = n_proj,   n_iter   = n_iter )  # Projected selectivity — replicate mean selectivity over the last 10 fitted years sel_proj <- project_selectivity(   data     = data_sim,   obj      = obj_sim,   first_yr = data_sim$last_yr - 9,   n_proj   = n_proj,   n_iter   = n_iter )  # Catch scenario: hold catch constant at the last observed year's level catch_ysf_proj <- array(0, dim = c(n_proj, data_sim$n_season, data_sim$n_fishery)) for (y in seq_len(n_proj)) {   catch_ysf_proj[y, , ] <- data_sim$catch_obs_ysf[data_sim$n_year, , ] } proj_mvn <- project_dynamics(   data      = data_sim,   object    = obj_sim,   mcmc      = NULL,          # triggers MVN path   n_proj    = n_proj,   n_iter    = n_iter,   rdev_y    = rdev_proj$rdev_y,   sel_fya   = sel_proj,   catch_ysf = catch_ysf_proj ) mcmc_fit <- SparseNUTS::sample_snuts(   obj         = obj_sim,   globals     = opal_globals(),   num_samples = 500,   num_warmup  = 1000,   chains      = n_chains_mcmc,   cores       = min(n_chains_mcmc, parallel::detectCores()),   metric      = "dense"     # ARIMA fitted to each posterior draw's rdev_y series   first_yr = data_sim$first_yr,    # match the estimated rdev period   n_proj   = n_proj,   n_iter   = n_iter ) proj_mcmc <- project_dynamics(   data        = data_sim,   object      = obj_sim,   mcmc        = mcmc_fit,      # text: Extract projected spawning biomass iteration compute quantile envelopes. Reading bridge point. MVN projections (blue): log_B0 log_cpue_q drawn MVN; rdev_y set conditional expectation given scalar draws, E[rdev_y | scalar_draw] = μ + Σ_{rdev,sc} Σ_{sc,sc}⁻¹ (draw − μ). accounts negative log_B0 ↔︎ rdev_y correlation Hessian (higher B₀ requires lower historical deviates fit declining trajectory) avoids Jensen’s-inequality bias — drawing 268 deviates simultaneously marginal distributions inflate E[SBY] ≈ 76 % MLE. bridge-point ribbon therefore aligns delta-method (sdreport) historical ribbon left panel, centred MLE spanning similar uncertainty. MCMC projections (orange): draw comes full joint posterior, including rdev_y. bridge-point spread therefore reflects actual posterior uncertainty current biomass state. cases, future process uncertainty (projected recruitment deviates selectivity) widens bands projection horizon. future uncertainty moderate? bigeye tuna mature slowly (spawning potential near zero ages 1–4), new recruits take several years contribute meaningfully spawning biomass. constant catch existing adult stock declines almost deterministically; divergence future recruitment selectivity uncertainty accumulates gradually. spa <- obj_sim$report()$spawning_potential_a  # [n_age] maturity × fecundity  # Helper: turn a list of do_dynamics() results into a long data frame. # number_ysa[1,,] is the initial state (= model end-state); include it as # proj_year = 0 so it bridges continuously to the historical trajectory. sbio_df <- function(proj_list, label) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(proj_list), function(i) {     dyn <- proj_list[[i]]     sb  <- sapply(1:(n_proj + 1), function(y) sum(dyn$number_ysa[y, 1, ] * spa))     data.frame(iter = i, proj_year = 0:n_proj, sbio = sb, method = label)   })) }  df_mvn  <- sbio_df(proj_mvn,       "MVN")   # plain list (no return_hist) df_mcmc <- sbio_df(proj_mcmc$dyn,  "MCMC")  # list(dyn=..., hist_sbio=...) df_all  <- rbind(df_mvn, df_mcmc) # MLE historical trajectory (from sdreport estimates, identical to rep_sim$spawning_biomass_y) hist_df <- data.frame(   timestep = seq_len(data_sim$n_year + 1),   sbio     = sbio_mle_sd[seq_len(data_sim$n_year + 1)] )  n_hist_show <- 100  # 100 quarters ≈ 25 years (covers the full 80-quarter recovery window) idx         <- (data_sim$n_year + 1 - n_hist_show + 1):(data_sim$n_year + 1)  # MVN historical ribbon: delta-method Gaussian CI from the Hessian (no Jensen bias). # Drawing all 268 rdev_y from their MVN marginals and propagating through the # exponential recruitment function inflates E[SBY] ≈ 76 % above the MLE — the # delta method avoids this by linearising at the MLE. df_hist_mvn <- data.frame(   timestep = idx,   med      = sbio_mle_sd[idx],   lo50     = sbio_mle_sd[idx] - qnorm(0.75) * sbio_se_sd[idx],   hi50     = sbio_mle_sd[idx] + qnorm(0.75) * sbio_se_sd[idx],   lo90     = sbio_mle_sd[idx] - qnorm(0.95) * sbio_se_sd[idx],   hi90     = sbio_mle_sd[idx] + qnorm(0.95) * sbio_se_sd[idx],   method   = "MVN" )  # MCMC historical ribbon: actual posterior trajectory quantiles hist_ribbon <- function(hist_sbio, label, n_show) {   n_ts <- ncol(hist_sbio)   idx2 <- (n_ts - n_show + 1):n_ts   do.call(rbind, lapply(idx2, function(t) {     v <- hist_sbio[, t]     data.frame(timestep = t,                med  = median(v, na.rm = TRUE),                lo50 = quantile(v, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), hi50 = quantile(v, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),                lo90 = quantile(v, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), hi90 = quantile(v, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),                method = label)   })) } df_hist_mcmc <- hist_ribbon(proj_mcmc$hist_sbio, "MCMC", n_hist_show)  df_hist_ribbon <- rbind(df_hist_mvn, df_hist_mcmc)  # Projection quantile ribbons (proj_year = 0 is the bridge / join point) df_ribbon <- df_all |>   # Some MCMC draws can produce NA SBIO values (e.g. when a draw yields an   # invalid initial state); drop them so quantile() doesn't error.   filter(!is.na(sbio)) |>   group_by(method, proj_year) |>   summarise(     med  = median(sbio, na.rm = TRUE),     lo50 = quantile(sbio, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),     hi50 = quantile(sbio, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),     lo90 = quantile(sbio, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),     hi90 = quantile(sbio, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),     .groups = "drop"   ) |>   filter(!is.na(med)) |>   mutate(timestep = data_sim$n_year + 1 + proj_year)  hist_zoom <- hist_df[hist_df$timestep > (data_sim$n_year + 1 - ",             n_gen + 1, n_gen + 5)) cat(sprintf("  MLE:       %s

code:
library(opal) library(RTMB) library(SparseNUTS) library(tidyverse) library(posterior)  theme_set(theme_bw())  # The MCMC fit is pre-computed and loaded from the package (see the # `mcmc-sampling` chunk, which is disabled); n_chains_mcmc must match the # number of chains used to produce the cached fit. n_chains_mcmc <- 8L data(opaka_data) data <- opaka_data if (is.null(data$n_index)) data$n_index <- 2L data$priors  <- NULL  # Anchor the growth curve at biological age 0 (SS3 indexes ages 0-43) data$A1      <- 0 data$A2      <- data$A1 + (data$n_age - 1) data$min_age <- 0 ages <- data$age_a <- seq(data$min_age, by = 1, length.out = data$n_age) data$sex_ratio <- rep(1, data$n_age)  # Length composition data (Comm = fleet 1, ResFish = fleet 3) data(opaka_lf) lf_wide <- opaka_lf %>%   tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(fishery, year, month, ts),                      names_from = bin, values_from = value, values_fill = 0) %>%   arrange(fishery, ts) data <- prep_lf_data(data, lf_wide,                      lf_keep_fisheries = c(1, 3),                      lf_var_adjust     = 1 / rep(1, data$n_fishery),                      lf_addtocomp      = 1e-10)  # Calendar years for the modelled period (1949-2023) calendar_years <- (1949 - 1) + data$years  # SS3-style recruitment bias-adjustment ramps init_cohort_years <- 1949 - (data$age_a - 1) data$init_bias_adj_a <- get_bias_adj_vector(   years = init_cohort_years, do_rec_bias_ramp = 1,   bias_years = c(1931, 1974, 2021.88, 2022.43), max_bias_adj = 0.869) data$bias_adj_y <- get_bias_adj_vector(   years = calendar_years, do_rec_bias_ramp = 1,   bias_years = c(1931, 1974, 2021.88, 2022.43), max_bias_adj = 0.869) data(opaka_parameters)  # Route the 1949 deviate to the age-0 cohort; shift 1950-2023 into rdev_y and # append a terminal 0 (see the opakapaka vignette for the full rationale). init_rdev_a <- rev(c(0.0206807,0.00321579,0.00372620,0.0043174,0.00500263,   0.00579674,0.00671727,0.00778422,0.00902081,0.0104539,0.0121143,0.0140375,   0.0162641,0.0188404,0.0218182,0.0252561,0.0292182,0.0337726,0.0389898,   0.0449362,0.0516662,0.0592049,0.0675236,0.0764992,0.0858443,0.0950047,   0.102706,0.107687,0.107712,0.0998349,0.0808137,0.0482339,0.00234443,   -0.0517563,-0.102395,-0.131458,-0.121101,-0.0714826,-0.00742166,-0.0109308,   -0.0385029,0.0366483,0.0165105,-0.166906)) init_rdev_a[1]   <- opaka_parameters$rdev_y[1] rdev_y_shifted   <- c(opaka_parameters$rdev_y[2:length(opaka_parameters$rdev_y)], 0.0)  parameters <- list(   log_B0         = 9,   log_h          = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_h),   log_sigma_r    = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_sigma_r),   log_cpue_q     = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_cpue_q),   log_cpue_tau   = rep(log(0.1), data$n_index),   log_cpue_omega = as.numeric(rep(opaka_parameters$log_cpue_omega, data$n_index)),   log_lf_tau     = as.numeric(log(rep(0.1, data$n_fishery))),   log_L1         = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_L1),   log_L2         = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_L2),   log_k          = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_k),   log_CV1        = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_CV1),   log_CV2        = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_CV2),   par_sel        = as.matrix(opaka_parameters$par_sel),   log_init_F_f   = c(log(0.0119122), rep(log(1e-8), data$n_fishery - 1)),   rdev_y         = rdev_y_shifted,   init_rdev_a    = init_rdev_a ) parameters$par_sel <- convert_ss3_selex_to_rtmb(parameters$par_sel,                                                 data$sel_type_f, data$len_mid)  data$priors <- get_priors(parameters = parameters, data = data) map_sel <- matrix(NA, nrow(parameters$par_sel), ncol(parameters$par_sel)) map_sel[1, 1:2]        <- c(1, 2)   # Comm logistic map_sel[3, c(1, 4, 6)] <- c(3, 4, 5) # ResFish double-normal map_sel <- as.vector(map_sel)  map <- list(   log_h          = factor(NA),   log_sigma_r    = factor(NA),   log_cpue_tau   = factor(rep(NA, data$n_index)),   log_cpue_omega = factor(rep(NA, data$n_index)),   log_lf_tau     = factor(rep(NA, length(parameters$log_lf_tau))),   log_L1  = factor(NA), log_L2 = factor(NA), log_k = factor(NA),   log_CV1 = factor(NA), log_CV2 = factor(NA),   par_sel      = factor(map_sel),   log_init_F_f = rep(factor(NA), data$n_fishery),   init_rdev_a  = as.factor(seq_len(data$n_age)),   rdev_y       = as.factor(seq_len(length(parameters$rdev_y))) ) data$lf_switch <- 1L   # multinomial length-composition likelihood  obj_lf <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data), parameters = parameters,                     map = map)  Lwr <- rep(-Inf, length(obj_lf$par)); Upr <- rep(Inf, length(obj_lf$par)) Lwr[grep("log_B0",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(1) Upr[grep("log_B0",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(exp(22)) Lwr[grep("log_cpue_q",  names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(0.001) Upr[grep("log_cpue_q",  names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(10) Lwr[grep("rdev_y",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- -5 Upr[grep("rdev_y",      names(obj_lf$par))] <-  5 Lwr[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_lf$par))] <- -5 Upr[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_lf$par))] <-  5 Lwr[grep("par_sel",     names(obj_lf$par))] <- -7 Upr[grep("par_sel",     names(obj_lf$par))] <-  7  control <- list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000) opt <- nlminb(obj_lf$par, obj_lf$fn, obj_lf$gr, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr,               control = control) opt <- nlminb(opt$par,    obj_lf$fn, obj_lf$gr, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr,               control = control) opt <- nlminb(opt$par,    obj_lf$fn, obj_lf$gr, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr,               control = control)  cat("Convergence:", opt$convergence, "
") cat("Max gradient:", max(abs(obj_lf$gr())), "
") cat("NLL:", opt$objective, "
") sdr       <- RTMB::sdreport(obj_lf) sdr_sum   <- summary(sdr, "report") sbio_rows <- which(rownames(sdr_sum) == "spawning_biomass_y") sbio_mle_sd <- sdr_sum[sbio_rows, "Estimate"] sbio_se_sd  <- sdr_sum[sbio_rows, "Std. Error"]  # Scalar parameter SEs from the inverse Hessian (for reference) H_lf   <- obj_lf$he(); Sigma <- solve(H_lf); SE_vec <- sqrt(diag(Sigma)) mu_vec <- obj_lf$env$last.par.best B0_est   <- obj_lf$report()$B0 term_idx <- data$n_year + 1 cat("B0 (MLE):", round(B0_est), "mt
") cat("Terminal SB:", round(sbio_mle_sd[term_idx]),     "+/-", round(sbio_se_sd[term_idx]), "mt (delta-method SE)
") cat("Terminal depletion SB/B0:", round(sbio_mle_sd[term_idx] / B0_est, 3), "
")

title: ’Opakapaka projections: MVN vs MCMC uncertainty
text: projection holds catch constant terminal year’s level across 10-year horizon. title: Copilot instructions for opal
text: core function R/model.R. RTMB-compatible closure : 1. Unpacks data + parameters via getAll(data, parameters) 2. Runs modular steps sequence: growth → PLA → weight--age → biology → selectivity → initial numbers → dynamics → priors → likelihoods 3. Aggregates NLL: nll = lp_prior + lp_rec + sum(lp_cpue) + sum(lp_lf) + sum(lp_wf) 4. Reports derived quantities via REPORT() (spawning biomass, numbers--age, etc.) Usage: RTMB::MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data), parameters = params, map = map) cmb(f, d) creates function(p) f(p, d).

title: Copilot instructions for opal
code: library(opal) data    <- wcpo_bet_data lf      <- wcpo_bet_lf params  <- wcpo_bet_parameters  # Prepare composition data data <- prep_lf_data(data, lf_wide = pivot_wider(...))  # Configure params  <- get_parameters(data) priors  <- get_priors(params, data) map     <- get_map(params) bounds  <- get_bounds(obj, params)  # Build AD object obj <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data), parameters = params, map = map)  # Optimize (double run for convergence) opt <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr, lower = bounds$lower, upper = bounds$upper) opt <- nlminb(opt$par, obj$fn, obj$gr, lower = bounds$lower, upper = bounds$upper)  # Diagnostics check_estimability(obj) get_cor_pairs(obj) sdreport(obj)  # Visualize plot_cpue(data, obj) plot_biomass_spawning(list(data), list(obj))  # Store fitted state and posterior output without serializing the RTMB object fit <- opal_fit(data, obj, opt, bounds = bounds, mcmc = mcmc_fit) save_opal_fit(fit, "fit.rds") fit <- read_opal_fit("fit.rds", strict = TRUE)

title: Copilot instructions for opal
text: R packages managed renv/. Run renv::activate() renv::restore() set . Key dependencies: RTMB, RTMBdist, SparseNUTS, ggplot2, dplyr, forecast Documentation: roxygen2-based. editing R/*.R files, regenerate devtools::document(). Tests: testthat edition 3. Run devtools::test(). Tests cover dynamics, growth, three likelihood types, selectivity, data prep, rebinning, utilities. title: Copilot instructions for opal
text: Run check_estimability(obj) fitting detect non-identifiable parameters via Hessian eigenvalue analysis. Run get_cor_pairs(obj, threshold = 0.95) find highly correlated parameter pairs. Use get_par_table() review initial vs estimated values, gradients, bounds proximity. Use obj$simulate() RTMB’s OBS() mechanism simulation-based diagnostics.

title: Copilot instructions for opal
text: AD safety first: adding modifying function receives AD values, include ADoverload("[<-") top. Test obj$fn(obj$par) returns finite value changes. Preserve exported API signatures: exported functions documented man/ used vignettes. Changing signatures requires updating roxygen docs, NAMESPACE, vignettes. Run tests changes: devtools::test() covers core components. adding new functionality, add corresponding tests tests/testthat/. Regenerate docs: editing roxygen comments R/ files, run devtools::document() update man/ NAMESPACE. Keep patches minimal: Modify one R/ file time, run devtools::test() devtools::check() validate. Composition data flow: modifying likelihood functions, understand full pipeline: raw data → prep_lf_data()/prep_wf_data() → flat vectors → likelihood function. lf_switch/wf_switch controls distribution used. Selectivity changes: modifying selectivity, update par_sel dimensions, get_map() (elements fixed), get_bounds() simultaneously.

title: 'Opakapaka Stock Assessment Data — opaka_data
text: Age time dimensions: age_a Vector integer ages (1:44). Length = 44. Internal opal ages mapping SS3 ages 0-43 (opal age = SS3 age - 1). n_age Number age classes (44). n_season Number seasons per year (1). n_fishery Number fisheries/fleets (3). n_year Number years model (75, representing 1949-2023). first_yr First year designation model (1, representing 1949). last_yr Last year designation model (75, representing 2023). years Vector model years (1:75). Length structure: len_bin_start First length bin lower edge (5 cm). len_bin_width Width length bin (5 cm). n_len Total number length bins (17). Catch data: first_yr_catch First year catch data (1). catch_units_f Numeric vector unit codes fishery (3 elements). fisheries use units = 1 (biomass). catch_obs_ysf Three-dimensional array observed catch (75 years x 1 season x 3 fisheries). Dimensions follow (year, season, fishery). Fleet 3 (ResFish survey) zero catch. CPUE data: cpue_switch Indicator CPUE inclusion (1 = included). cpue_data Data.table 82 rows 8 columns containing CPUE observations two fleets: year: Calendar year (1949-2023) month: Observation month (7 Comm fleet, 1 ResFish) ts: Sequential timestep (1-75) fishery: Fleet identifier (1 = Comm, 3 = ResFish) index: Integer index identifier (1 Comm, 2 ResFish) metric: Data type ("cpue") units: Unit code (1 biomass) value: CPUE observations se: Log-space standard error (0.2 Comm, 0.15 ResFish) Comm fleet (fleet 1) covers 1949-2023 (75 obs). ResFish survey (fleet 3) covers 2017-2023 (7 obs). Biological parameters: lw_a Length-weight allometric coefficient (1.75e-05). lw_b Length-weight allometric exponent (2.99). maturity Maturity length vector (17 elements). Logistic maturity probabilities data length bin midpoint (Mat50 = 40.7 cm, slope = -2.26). fecundity Fecundity length vector (17 elements). Fecundity equals weight length bin midpoint (fecundity option: eggs = Wt). M Natural mortality age vector (44 elements). Constant instantaneous rate (0.135) across ages. Growth reference ages (Schnute parameterization): A1 Reference age L1 (1). Corresponds SS3 age 0. A2 Reference age L2 (44 = n_age). Corresponds SS3 age 43. Selectivity: sel_type_f Selectivity function type fishery (3 elements). Integer codes: 1 = logistic, 2 = double-normal, 3 = double Richards. Priors: priors List 8 Bayesian prior specifications, containing: type: Prior distribution type ("none" = uninformative) par1: First parameter (NA type = "none") par2: Second parameter (NA type = "none") index: Parameter index model Priors cover: log_B0, log_cpue_q, par_sel, log_L1, log_L2, log_k, log_CV1, log_CV2.

text: Fleet 1 (Comm) Commercial fishery. Catch fleet logistic selectivity. CPUE length composition data available 1949-2023. Fleet 2 (Non_comm) Non-commercial fishery. CPUE length composition data available 2017-2023.

title: Double-normal selectivity as a function of length (SS3 pattern 24, full form) — sel_double_normal
text: x Numeric vector length-bin midpoints. par Numeric vector length 6 containing selectivity parameters. par[1] () Peak location (real line). Transformed via mean(x) + * sd(x), = 0 places peak mean(x). par[2] (b) Plateau width (real line). Controls distance peak start descending limb via logistic transform available range: peak + bin_width + (0.99 * max(x) - peak - bin_width) / (1 + exp(-b)). par[3] (c) Ascending width (real line, log-space). Actual denominator = exp(c) * sd(x)^2. par[4] (d) Descending width (real line, log-space). Actual denominator = exp(d) * sd(x)^2. par[5] (e) Initial selectivity (real line, logit-space). Transformed via 1 / (1 + exp(-e)), e = 0 gives initial selectivity 0.5, large negative values give ~0, large positive values give ~1. par[6] (f) Final selectivity (real line, logit-space). transform e.

what: Double Richards selectivity as a function of length — sel_double_richards
title: Double Richards selectivity as a function of length — sel_double_richards
text: smooth, six-parameter curve formed multiplying ascending generalized-logistic (Richards) limb one minus descending Richards limb: $$(1 + \exp(-z_1))^{-1/\gamma_1} [1 - (1 + \exp(-z_2))^{-1/\gamma_2}].$$ Parameters real line transformed follows: par[1] Ascending 50% point: mean(len) + par[1] * sd(len). par[2] Ascending width: exp(par[2]) * sd(len). par[3] Ascending shape: gamma1 = exp(par[3]). par[4] Descending 50% point ascending 50% point plus exp(par[4]) * sd(len). par[5] Descending width: exp(par[5]) * sd(len). par[6] Descending shape: gamma2 = exp(par[6]). Maunder parameterization recovered alpha_k = L50_k + log(2^gamma_k - 1) / beta_k beta_k = log(19) / width_k. peak can one limbs overlap; intentionally rescaled. either shape parameter tends negative infinity, limb tends Gompertz curve 50% point. Large shape values flatten limb toward 0.5 (par[3] = par[6] = 7, curve approximately 0.25). Mapping par[3] par[6] zero gives four-parameter double-logistic curve. Suggested bounds columns 3 6 c(-5, 5); use existing par_sel bounds remaining columns.

text: Age time dimensions: age_a Vector integer ages (1:40). Length = 40. n_age Number age classes (40). n_season Number seasons per year (1). n_fishery Number fisheries/fleets (15). n_year Number years model (268, equivalent 67 years x 4 quarters). first_yr First year designation model (1, representing 1952). last_yr Last year designation model (268, representing 2018). years Vector model years (1:268). Length structure: len_bin_start First length bin lower edge (10 cm). len_bin_width Width length bin (2 cm). n_len Total number length bins (95). Catch data: first_yr_catch First year catch data (1). catch_units_f Numeric vector unit codes fishery (15 elements). 1 = metric tons (fisheries 8-14), 2 = thousands fish (fisheries 1-7, 15). catch_obs_ysf Three-dimensional array observed catch (268 years x 1 season x 15 fisheries). Dimensions follow (year, season, fishery). Units follow catch_units_f. CPUE data: cpue_switch Indicator CPUE inclusion (1 = included, typically fishery 15). n_index Number distinct CPUE/survey indices (integer). cpue_data Tibble 268 rows 9 columns containing standardized CPUE observations: year: Calendar year (1952-2018) month: Quarter month (2, 5, 8, 11 Q1-Q4) ts: Sequential timestep (1-268) fishery: Fleet identifier (usually 15 survey fleet) index: Integer index identifier (1, 2, ..., n_index) metric: Data type ("cpue") units: Unit code (typically 2 fishery 15) value: Normalized CPUE observations se: Log-space standard error CPUE observations Biological parameters: lw_a Length-weight allometric coefficient (6.48e-05). lw_b Length-weight allometric exponent (2.78). maturity Maturity length vector (95 elements). Ogive-based maturity probabilities length bin. fecundity Fecundity length vector (95 elements). Relative fecundity length bin. M Natural mortality age vector (40 elements). Age-specific instantaneous mortality rates. Age bounds: A1 Minimum age credibility interval (1). A2 Maximum age credibility interval (40). Selectivity: sel_type_f Selectivity function type fishery (15 elements). Integer codes representing selectivity curve shapes: 1 = logistic, 2 = double-normal, 3 = double Richards. Priors: priors List 8 Bayesian prior specifications, containing: type: Prior distribution type ("normal", etc.) par1: First parameter (mean location) par2: Second parameter (std dev scale) index: Parameter index model Priors cover: log_B0, log_cpue_q, par_sel, log_L1, log_L2, log_k, log_CV1, log_CV2. Length composition data: lf_minbin Integer vector (n_fishery). Per-fishery minimum bin index lower-tail aggregation. Bins 1 lf_minbin[f] summed bin lf_minbin[f]. Default 1 (aggregation). lf_maxbin Integer vector (n_fishery). Per-fishery maximum bin index upper-tail aggregation. Bins lf_maxbin[f] n_len summed bin lf_maxbin[f]. Default n_len (aggregation).
